title: Daulat Khan’s Sons Rise, Then Fall under Bairam Khan

blocks.text: The page continues the account of Daulat Khan's household by saying that Daulat Khan's wives received Guru Nanak's blessing and then bore the sons they had long desired. Those sons are named and positioned as the fruit of grace before the narrative shifts to their political advancement.

As the four boys mature, they enter service and become nawabs or high officials at the Delhi court under the Lodhi order. Their rise links Guru Nanak's blessing with worldly prominence, but only briefly, because court politics remain unstable and dangerous.

After Sikandar Lodhi's line passes on, Bairam Khan's arrogance ruins experienced governance, and Daulat Khan's sons are among those destroyed in the ensuing violence. The page therefore pairs fulfilled blessing with sudden reversal, preparing Daulat Khan's desperate appeal for justice.
